doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Learning standards on cruise ships and settling in Pittsburgh
summary: Older ship musicians taught him tunes before the internet; he later moved to Pittsburgh with a cover band and met Roger Humphries.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Learned how to be punctual. Learned how to front a band. Learned a bunch of standards without the internet and real books or anything. Nineties.
Okay. How did you learn them if you didn’t have the internet.

I’d have older guys show them to me. Because when we came onto the ship, I remember the first ship I came onto in a quartet, the other band was guys that, they knew a million tunes. And they were thirty, forty years older than us. So they would be a resource. They might have — I remember that guy having a stack of real books but we didn’t have that. He had a stack of real books. So that was one resource. But also you could just catch them after their set, because I would figure things out and say, “Hey what’s the bridge to” such and such. And they would just show me you know. So I left that and I went back to Pittsburgh and started doing my thing there. And my idea was to go to New York. I had friends that were moving to New York. But keep in mind I’m from Wheeling, West Virginia. So I was thrilled to get that cruise ship gig. You know there was a big possibility in my mind that I would never get out of West Virginia. So I got, the thing that helped me to move to Pittsburgh was I got a gig with a cover band so I could move to Pittsburgh. And then I started to come on the jazz scene.
